s: Who is the founder of the "Navdanya" movement for seed, food, water, land and knowledge sovereignty for people?
x: Vandana Shiva founded Navdanya for seed, food, water, land and knowledge sovereignty; Rajendra Singh is the 'waterman', Sandeep Pandey and Mallika Sarabhai are other activists.

s: Samir, who attended prominently the Asian Social Forum (Hyderabad) and the World Social Forum, is also director of the Third World Forum. Where is the Third World Forum?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Dakar (Senegal)); it is added as option 5.
Samir Amin directed the Third World Forum in Dakar, Senegal, from 1980; it is not in London, Belgium, Dar-es-Salaam or Kuwait (Belgium hosts CETRI at Louvain-la-Neuve, a different body).

s: The Asian Social Forum was held in Hyderabad in January 2003. Where was the European Social Forum held in November 2002?
x: The first European Social Forum was held in Florence, Italy, in November 2002; Hyderabad hosted the Asian Social Forum in January 2003.

s: Jan Bremen referred to migrant labour as
x: Jan Breman termed migrant labourers 'footloose labour' (Footloose Labour, 1996).

s: The expected negative effects of MNCs are listed. Which of the following list I out of place?
o: Crowding out domestic saving and investment
x: Large dividend remittances, crowding out domestic saving and influence in key sectors are negatives of MNCs; fulfilling export obligations is a benefit, so it is out of place.

s: "Culture is the part created by man in the environment". Who said this ?
x: 'Culture is the man-made part of the environment' is M.J. Herskovits's definition (Man and His Works, 1948). Tylor defined culture as a 'complex whole' of knowledge, belief, art, morals, law and custom, and Malinowski as inherited artefacts, goods and ideas, so 'None of the above'.

s: Who first mentioned the concept of "social evolution" ?
x: Herbert Spencer was among the first to study society from an evolutionary point of view; his Social Statics (1851) already framed social evolution, and he coined 'survival of the fittest'. Comte gave the law of three stages, Lester Ward 'telesis' (printed key: Lester F. Ward).

s: Who said "Society is a fabric of social relations"?
x: MacIver and Page called society 'a web (fabric) of social relationships'. Weber is linked with social action, Veblen with the leisure class and Marx with class struggle.

s: "Society is like a weaving work of social relations." With whom of the following is this comment associated?
x: 'Society is a web of social relationships' is MacIver's definition (MacIver and Page, Society); it is not from Marx, Durkheim or Weber.

s: Who proposed the concept of "Social capillary" ?
x: 'Social capillarity' was coined by the French demographer Arsène Dumont (Dépopulation et Civilisation, 1890): the pursuit of upward mobility makes families limit births, like liquid rising in a capillary tube. Louis Dumont (Homo Hierarchicus) is the caste scholar, a trap (printed key: Louis Dumont).

s: What kind of authority does the tribal leader exercise ?
x: A tribal chief's authority rests on custom and tradition, so it is Weber's traditional authority, not rational-legal or magical power.

s: Which of the following is included in Weber's typology of action ?
o: Rational action with respect to purpose, rational action with respect to values, emotional action, conventional action
Conventional Action, Populist Action, Rational Action
x: Weber's four types of social action are instrumentally (goal) rational, value-rational, affective (emotional) and traditional (conventional).

s: According to Karl Marx, class membership is based on what ?
x: For Marx, class is fixed by one's position in the relations of production (owners vs non-owners of the means of production), not by authority or prestige (Weber).

s: Who among the following termed sociology as "social physics" ?
x: Auguste Comte first called the new science 'social physics' and later renamed it 'sociology' (1838), partly because Quetelet had used 'social physics' for statistics.

s: Who included India in the Asiatic Mode of Production?
x: Karl Marx placed India in the 'Asiatic mode of production' (writings on India 1853-58): village communities without private landed property under a despotic state. Weber wrote The Religion of India (printed key: Max Weber).

s: What is the habit of a person occupying a position of traditional authority based on a belief in holiness and obedience?
x: Authority resting on belief in the sanctity of age-old custom and obedience to its holder is Weber's traditional authority.

s: Who is the author of the book 'Sociology of Economic Life'?
x: The Sociology of Economic Life (1963) is by Neil J. Smelser.

s: Who described Sociology as the encyclopedic science of society?
x: Comte (and Spencer) saw sociology as a synthetic, encyclopaedic science of society, the queen of the sciences; Sorokin and MacIver held the specialist (formal) view.

s: It is said that "Religion is an intoxicant of people". Who said?
x: Marx called religion 'the opium of the people' (intoxicant), in his Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right (1844).

s: Who wrote 'Communist Manifesto'?
x: The Communist Manifesto (1848) was written jointly by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, so 'Marx and Engels' is the full answer (printed key: Marx alone).

s: Who said "Religion is an intoxicant for people"?
x: 'Religion is the opium (intoxicant) of the people' is Karl Marx's remark, not Gandhi's or Lenin's.

s: Who said 'Religion is a heart for the heartless'?
x: Marx called religion 'the sigh of the oppressed creature, the heart of a heartless world' and 'the opium of the people' (1844).

s: According to whom 'the existence of strong personal attachments and the fact of death, which of all human events is the most upsetting and disorganizing to man's calculations, are perhaps the main sources of religious belief'?
x: Malinowski's functionalist theory held that strong personal attachments and death, the most upsetting of human events, are the main sources of religious belief.

s: Who among the following wrote The Communist Manifesto along with Karl Marx?
x: The Communist Manifesto (1848) was written jointly by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.

s: Scientific socialism is attributed to
x: Scientific socialism is attributed to Karl Marx (with Engels), as against the earlier utopian socialism.

s: Which one of the following is the central theme of ‘The Communist Manifesto’ written by Marx and Engels?
x: The Manifesto opens: 'The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles' – class struggle is its central theme.

x: Ferdinand Tonnies distinguished Gemeinschaft (community) from Gesellschaft (association) in 1887.

x: Aristotle wrote in the Politics that man is by nature a social (political) animal.

s: Who proposed the conflict theory?
x: Ralf Dahrendorf developed modern conflict theory (Class and Class Conflict in Industrial Society, 1959); Parsons and Spencer are functionalists.

s: Who used the concept of recruitment roles?
x: S.F. Nadel (The Theory of Social Structure, 1957) used the concept of recruitment roles (how persons are recruited to roles, by ascription or achievement). Linton gave ascribed and achieved status, Parsons pattern variables, Homans exchange theory (printed key: Homans).

s:
Consider the following theories:

A. The theory of positivism proposed by Comte

B. Theory of division of labor proposed by Durkheim

C. Spencer's theory of emotional similarity
Which is the correct historical timeline for the above theories ?
x: Comte's positivism (Course of Positive Philosophy, 1830-42) came first, then Spencer's evolutionary theory (1850s-60s), then Durkheim's Division of Labour (1893): A, C, B.

s: 'Society is a web of social relations' said?
x: MacIver (with Page) defined society as 'a web of social relationships'. Moved to the basic concepts row.

x: The item is garbled: 'Nepotism is bad for any relationship' carries no question, and the options (inter-group, equal-group, intergroup, community relations) repeat each other, so no answer can be established.

o: Using physical strength for self benefit
Mass violence leading to disruption of social life
Existence of fighting groups in the society
A person or group forcibly imposes its opinion on another or another group
x: Coercion means a person or group forcibly imposing its will or opinion on another person or group; mere violence or the existence of fighting groups is not coercion itself.

s: When we decide our floor, what is the group we compare ourselves with?
x: The group we compare ourselves with to judge our own position or behaviour is a reference group (Merton); people identify with it even without belonging to it. Peer, kinship and secondary groups need not be the standard, and the stem ('decide our floor') is garbled.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP

Geographic territory and uniformity of conduct
Likeness and differences between the group members
Geographic territory and sense of solidarity
x: MacIver and Page name two bases of a community: locality (a definite territory) and community sentiment (we-feeling, a sense of solidarity), i.e. option D. 'A group sharing the basic conditions of a common life' (A) is MacIver's definition of community, not its features (printed key: A).

x: 'Men are stronger than women' is a belief: a proposition held to be true (here a stereotype), not an oath, value or approval.

o: To study the best model in the society
x: The main purpose of the sociologist is to study society scientifically, describing and explaining it; changing or integrating society is the task of reformers and policy.

s: Who developed social distance as a technique for measuring attitudes ?
x: Emory Bogardus developed the social distance scale (1925) to measure attitudes towards other groups. Thurstone and Guttman built other attitude scales; Lundberg was a sociometrist.

src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
s: Social structure, culture and personality combined together form
x: Social structure, culture and personality together make up a social system (Talcott Parsons: social, cultural and personality systems).

x: Institutionalisation is the process by which conventions, norms and rules become established and stable in social forms; socialisation is learning them.

s: Which of the following is true about sociology?
o: It is the scientific study of society
It is concerned with the behavior of individuals in society
It studies groups and their organizations
Its purpose is to eliminate evils in the society
x: Sociology is the scientific study of society (A), the standard definition; it studies groups and behaviour in society too, but its aim is not to eliminate evils (printed key: B, which is only part of its scope).

s: Language is the product of this
x: Language is learned and transmitted socially, so it is a product of culture, not of biological heritage.

s: Which of the following characteristics best represents the difference between animal society and human society?
x: Culture, the learned way of life passed on by symbols, best separates human from animal society; language is part of culture.

s: The notion that man is stronger than woman is a
x: 'Man is stronger than woman' is a belief, a proposition accepted as true (the same item elsewhere is keyed 'belief'); 'Trust' here translates belief (nammakam). A value is a judgement of what is desirable, not a factual claim (printed key: Value).

src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa

x: A painter's role exists by itself; father, teacher and officer are defined only in relation to a counter-role (child, student, subordinate).

x: L.L. Thurstone's equal-appearing interval scale (1928) measures attitudes in psychology and sociology.

x: Tradition, language and customs are components of a culture; the economy is a separate institution, not an essential component of culture.

Assertion (A) and the other as
Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The concept of National Integration involves political, economic, social, cultural and psychological dimensions and inter-relation between them.
Reason (R) : The National Integration Council was constituted in 1961 on the principle of ‘Unity in Diversity’.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
x: National integration has political, economic, social, cultural and psychological dimensions (A true), and the National Integration Council was constituted in 1961 to promote unity in diversity (R true). But R only states when and why the NIC was set up; it does not explain why integration is multi-dimensional, so 'R is not the correct explanation' (printed key: R is the correct explanation).

s: The biggest museum of the country depicting the story of the development of human civilisation and also known as Indira Gandhi Manav Sangrahalaya is situated in
x: The Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (National Museum of Mankind), depicting the story of human evolution and culture, is in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.

s: Pongal is the festival of which state?
x: Pongal is the harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated in mid-January; Andhra Pradesh celebrates the same season as Sankranti.

s: It is said that 'the place of women in any society is the main symbol of the culture of that society'. Who said this?
x: The statement that the place of women is the main symbol of a society's culture is credited to K.M. Panikkar (printed key kept; not verified). A.S. Altekar, not among the options, made a similar point in The Position of Women in Hindu Civilisation.

s:
Two statements labelled as
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) are given. Consider both the statements carefully and select your answer on the basis of the given options.
Assertion (A): Contemporary Indian literature reflects the complexities of societal shifts and cultural dynamics in the India.
Reason (R): Through themes of identity, gender, and social critique, Indian authors engage with the evolving fabric of Indian society, blending tradition with modernity in their literary expressions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false and R is true.

x: Contemporary Indian literature reflects social and cultural change (A), and it does so precisely through themes of identity, gender and social critique blending tradition and modernity (R), so R explains A.

s: Which of the following religions does not have a specific text (scripture)?
x: Hinduism has no single founding scripture (many texts: Vedas, Upanishads, Gita); Judaism has the Torah, Christianity the Bible, Islam the Quran. Moved to Indian society.

s: Who among the following coined the concept of 'Primordial primary' group?
x: Edward Shils (1957) introduced 'primordial' ties and groups for the blood bonds of the family; the 'primary group' itself is C.H. Cooley's term ('C.H. wage' is a misprint), and George Homans worked on small-group exchange, not primordial groups.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: Family, School, Club, Gymnasium, Sports and games etc, belongs to which group?
x: In the textbook classification by duration, groups like family, school, club and sports teams are permanent groups, as against temporary groups like a crowd or audience.

s: Which of the following is an example of a community ?
x: No key can be settled: in MacIver's sociology a club and a religious establishment are associations (organised for specific interests), not communities, so the printed key 'a club related to sports' contradicts the textbook distinction; family and kinship groups are treated as both community and association by different authors, so the question has no single defensible answer.

s: When a group of people gets excited and engages in or prepares to engage in violent action, what is the group called?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Mob); it is added as option 5.
An excited crowd that engages in or prepares for violent action is a mob. A crowd is any temporary gathering, a gang is a small organised group and an aggregation is a mere collection, so no printed option fits.

s: Which of the following is not a secondary group characteristic?
x: Membership of secondary groups is voluntary, so compulsory membership is not their characteristic.

s:
Which of the following are characteristics associated with a primary group?

A. Small size

B. Self-interest

C. Comparison in background

D. Common interests
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
x: A primary group (Cooley) is small, has similarity of background and shared common interests, with intimate face-to-face ties. Self-interest marks secondary groups and associations, not primary groups.

s: A group of people organized for a particular need is called
x: A group deliberately organised to meet a particular need or purpose is an association or formal organisation, so "organization" is correct. A community is a group of people sharing a common life in a locality, not one formed for a particular need (printed key: community).

s: The group, ever more conscious of its unity is made
o: When its members have common interests
When its members live relatively isolated
When it is at breaking point
x: A group becomes most conscious of its unity when another group threatens it, as external threat strengthens in-group solidarity (sociology).

s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a secondary group?
x: Secondary groups are relatively large, formal and impersonal; physical proximity (face-to-face contact) is the classic condition of a primary group, so it is not a feature of a secondary group. Largeness in size IS a feature, so the printed key is wrong (permanency and compulsory membership are also weak features of secondary groups, but physical proximity is the textbook contrast).

s: Conflict is a modified form of this
x: In sociology conflict is treated as an intensified, personal form of competition (Park and Burgess); cooperation is its opposite and 'struggle' is not the textbook term.

s: Which of the following is not a means of informal control?
x: The police is an agency of formal control (law, coercion); family, community and social media (gossip, ridicule) are informal controls.

s:
Consider the following statements on the 'social capital'

A. Interconnected network of relationships between individuals and groups

B. Trust levels in the networks or ties

C. Amount of financial investment made by the individuals to the common pool

D. Resources or benefits gained by virtue of social ties and social participation
Which of the above statements are related to the 'three dimensions of social capital'?
x: Social capital has structural (networks of relationships), relational (trust) and resource (benefits from ties and participation) dimensions; individual financial investment is economic, not social, capital.

s: Which of the following is an example of anticipatory socialization ?
o: Parents to socialize their unmarried daughters to make proper adjustments to their husbands' families in post-marriage life.
A housewife teaching her maids how to do household chores.
To train soldiers to fight the enemy.
A manager to participate in a training program to improve his communication skills.
x: Anticipatory socialisation is learning the norms of a group or role one expects to join – e.g. preparing daughters for life in their husbands' families.

s: The process of socialization is
o: Begins at a very young age and ends in adolescence
Contributes to the learning of an individual's disciplined lifestyle
Society helps to reproduce itself socially and biologically.
For children it helps in finding good relationships.
x: Socialisation is the lifelong process through which society reproduces itself socially and culturally; it does not end in adolescence.

s: Why is language important to human society?
o: It easily fulfills man's need for expression
Adi Aatavika created man as a supreme being
x: Language is a social product whose chief importance to society is that it makes communication and so social relations possible. It is not merely a human invention or a vehicle for individual expression, and the 'Adi Aatavika' option is a myth, not a reason.

src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
s: Who wrote "Modernization of Indian Tradition"?
x: Yogendra Singh wrote Modernization of Indian Tradition (1973), analysing orthogenetic (internal) and heterogenetic (external) sources of change.

s: Who wrote the book "Modernisation of Indian Tradition" ?
x: Modernisation of Indian Tradition (1973) is by Yogendra Singh. Srinivas wrote Social Change in Modern India, S.C. Dube Indian Village.

s: H.S. Maine used the __ approach to study the Indian Joint Family.
x: Henry Maine studied the Indian joint family from classical Hindu law texts (Ancient Law, 1861; Village Communities, 1871), so his approach is classed as Indological (textual) rather than structural-functional, Marxist or feminist.

at: Both (Sociology, Psychology, law) & (Public Health and Community Development)
x: The scope of social work draws on sociology, psychology and law and covers public health and community development.

s: A family formed based on blood relationship is called this.
x: A family built on blood ties (parents, children, siblings) is the consanguine family ('united blood family' in translation); the conjugal family rests on the marriage bond.

s: When authority in a family is attributed to a woman it is called
x: A family where authority lies with a woman is matriarchal (options A and B repeat it). Matrilineal refers only to descent through the mother, and matriarchy is more theoretical than empirical.

s: What is the residence where the couple has the option to live with either the bride's parents or the groom's parents?
x: When the couple may live with either the bride's or the groom's parents, residence is ambilocal (bilocal). Neolocal = a new home; duolocal = each spouse in own natal home.

s: What kind of joint family is 'Okka'?
x: Among the Coorgs, the okka (M.N. Srinivas, Religion and Society among the Coorgs) is a patrilineal, patrilocal joint family owning land in common.

s: What are the rules of residence where a married couple goes to live with their mother-in-law's brother?
x: Residence with the husband's mother's brother is avunculocal ('matula' = maternal uncle).

s: Family into which a person is born and socialized. This is called
x: The family into which one is born and socialised is the family of orientation; the one founded by one's marriage is the family of procreation.

s: Based on this family is divided into monogamous family and polygamous family?
x: Monogamous and polygamous families are classified by the form of marriage (number of mates).

s: Which of the following correctly defines a family formed as a result of marriage and consequent children?
x: The family formed by marriage and the couple's children is the family of procreation.

s: Which type of residence does not support the formation of an extended family?
x: Neolocal residence (a new home away from both parents) does not support an extended family; viri-, uxori- and avunculocal residence keep kin together.

s: What do you call a family where there is division between 'Biological father' and 'social father'?
x: Separation of the biological father (genitor) from the social father (pater) occurs in polyandrous, i.e. polygamous, families, as among the Toda, where a rite fixes the social father (printed key: Patriarchal family).

s: Which of the following is correct for patriarchal society ?
x: A patriarchal society is male-dominated: the oldest male holds authority.

s:
Which of the following does not belong to the orientation family?

A. Parents

B. Wife / Husband

C. Siblings
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (B only); it is added as option 5.
The family of orientation is one's family of birth: parents and siblings. The wife or husband belongs to the family of procreation, so only B does not belong; no printed code says 'B only' (A, B, C wrongly drops parents and siblings too).

s: The offspring (children) of the same parents are called
x: Children of the same parents are siblings.

s: In which family is dominated by the children, where their wishes are formed as a family system, such a family is called this?
x: Printed key kept: a child-centred family run around the children's wishes is called an affection-centred (filiocentric) family.

s: Family of orientation is this type of family
o: What we should establish through marriage
We are a family of birth
x: The family of orientation is the family of birth.

s: Which of the following is not a basis for family classification?
x: Families are classified by inheritance, residence, authority, descent, marriage and structure – not by religion. Off-topic (society), moved.

s: The term 'Unstable Family' was first used by
x: Frederic Le Play classified families into patriarchal, stem and unstable types; the 'unstable family' is his term.

s: Which of the following is the first agency of socialization?
x: The family is the first (primary) agency of socialisation; school, peer group and community come later.

s: What is the necessary reason for the emergence of family?
x: The family emerged to meet sexual, economic and reproductive needs together, so 'all these' (MacIver: sex need, procreation, economic need).

s: Who divided family activities into essential and non-essential activities?
x: MacIver and Page divided family functions into essential (stable satisfaction of sex need, procreation and rearing, a home) and non-essential (religious, educational, economic, health, recreation). Ogburn and Nimkoff listed seven functions.

s: Main social function of family
x: The family's social functions include reproduction (population replacement), status ascription and socialisation, so 'all of the above'.

s:
Consider the following statement:

B. Family has lost most of its traditional functions.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

A is wrong and B is correct
x: The family is no longer the main unit of production (now a consumption unit) and has lost most traditional functions to outside agencies (Ogburn's 'loss of functions'), so both are correct.

s: The single most important socializing agency in all forms of society
x: The family is the single most important socialising agency in every society.

s: Duties in Modern Family
x: Many traditional duties of the family (education, care, production) have moved to schools, the state and markets, so the functions of the modern family are decreasing. Off-topic, moved to book 2 row 106.

s: Which of the following is NOT a family activity in an industrial society?
o: Imparting social values and culture to children
x: In an industrial society production moves out of the home into factories, so the family is no longer a production unit; it still socialises, educates and consumes.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: The process of personality development is completed in how many Stages according to Erikson.
x: Erik Erikson's psychosocial theory has eight stages, from trust vs mistrust (infancy) to integrity vs despair (old age).

s: The statuses of husbands and wives can be said in this way?
x: The statuses of husband and wife are functional (complementary) statuses, each defined by the role it plays in the family.

s: Who among the following argued that people of India lived mostly in small and simple households?
x: A.M. Shah (The Household Dimension of the Family in India, 1973) showed from census and historical data that most Indians always lived in small and simple households; the large joint household was confined to some sections.

s: Who said that joint family is an extended kinship group in India?
x: Irawati Karve defined the joint family as a group living under one roof, eating from one hearth, holding property in common and related as a type of kindred, i.e. an extended kinship group.

s: Author of the book 'Marriage and Family in India'?
x: Marriage and Family in India (1955) is by K.M. Kapadia, the pioneer of family studies in India.

s: A.M. Shah argued for a conceptual distinction between family and
x: A.M. Shah (The Household Dimension of the Family in India) insisted on distinguishing the family from the household.

s: Milton Singer's research on ___ focused on the resilience of traditional family and values.
x: Milton Singer's study of industrial leaders in Madras (When a Great Tradition Modernizes) found the joint family and its values resilient.

s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a joint family?
x: A joint family has co-residence, common property and common worship; private ownership of property is not its characteristic.

s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a joint family?
o: All members living in one household
Members need not be related to each other
The entire property belongs to the family
x: Joint family members live in one household, hold property in common and pool income, and are related by kinship; 'members need not be related' is false.

s: 'Dayabhaga' is generally practiced in which state?
x: The Dayabhaga school (Jimutavahana) prevails in Bengal and Assam; the Mitakshara school governs the rest of India.

s: In which year Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act introduced?
x: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act was passed in 1956 with the Hindu Succession and Minority and Guardianship Acts.

x: The Hindu Minority and Guardianship (Amendment) Bill, 2016 (amending sections 6 and 7 to give mothers equal guardianship) was introduced in 2016 as a private member's bill.

s: Under Family Courts Act 1984, Family Courts can be set up by
x: Under the Family Courts Act, 1984 the State Government, after consulting the High Court, sets up family courts (mandatory in cities over one million).

s: Who among the following expressed the opinion that family is the ideal instrument in an exploitative society?
x: David Cooper (The Death of the Family, 1971) called the family an ideological conditioning device, the ideal instrument of an exploitative society. Engels linked the monogamous family to private property but did not use this phrase (printed key: Engels).

s:
Morgan identified five different family forms. They are:

A. Syndyasmian

B. Punaluan

C. A united family

D. Monogamous

E. Patriarchal family
Select the answer from the codes given below and indicate their correct order as mentioned by Morgan.
x: L.H. Morgan (Ancient Society, 1877) gave five forms in order: consanguine ('united'), punaluan, syndyasmian, patriarchal, monogamian, i.e. C, B, A, E, D.

s: A Nair family is called
x: A Nair matrilineal joint family is the tharavad (tharwad). Ghotul is the Muria youth dormitory; Nokna and Illam are distractors.

s: In which of the following tribes does property inherit to the youngest daughter?
x: Among the Khasi of Meghalaya the youngest daughter (ka khadduh) inherits the ancestral property.

s: Which of the following is the main factor behind the disintegration of the joint family system in India?
x: Industrialisation and urbanisation (migration for jobs, wage work, small urban housing) are the main forces breaking up the joint family; laws, women's education and freedom are secondary factors.

s: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a modern family?
x: The modern family shows financial independence of members, decline of religious control and greater freedom for women; increased religious feeling is not its trait.
